title: Adaptive Response Synthesizer: JSON-mode contract lint & compatibility playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible test harness and operational playbook for adaptive JSON-mode enforcement that exercises constrained decoders, schema fallbacks, and compatibility with legacy 'soft-json' clients. The goal is to detect regressions across model versions and runtime kernel selections and provide deterministic recovery paths for partial/invalid stream emissions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated end-to-end test suite that runs against production model snapshots and flags schema violations with example payloads
Playbook document that lists prioritized recovery strategies (lint, repair, deterministic fallback) and clear rollback criteria
Instrumentation added to streaming infra to record token-level schema-violation signals and repair latency metrics
Compatibility matrix documenting behavior for legacy clients and a sample shim proving backwards-compatible outputs
test_plan: Build a synthetic workload generator that emits 2000 diverse prompts per run (mix of chat, function call, and streaming partial outputs)
Run constrained-decoder variations (strict grammar-first, probabilistic-constrained, greedy-with-repair) across 3 model weights and 2 quantization profiles
Inject token corruption scenarios (prefix truncation, interleaved toolcall markers, mid-stream latency spikes) and validate recovery heuristics
Measure false-positive and false-negative rates for the JSON linter with labeled ground truth corpus
Schedule nightly canary runs and a weekly matrix run that posts results to the structured-output dashboard
decisions: Adopt a two-stage enforcement: lightweight streaming linter in the realtime path + stronger post-stream repair/validation in the async path
Prefer a grammar-first constrained decoder for high-SLO low-variance routes and a probabilistic-constrained decoder for throughput-optimized routes
Expose a compatibility flag for legacy clients that applies a best-effort reformatting shim rather than hard rejection
Telemetry will emit a new metric 'jsonmode.schema_violation_rate' and a sample payload artifact (anonymized) when violation rate > 0.5%
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement reduces downstream parsing errors but increases tail latency and token-level overhead
Best-effort repair improves UX for legacy clients but can mask regressions if used as a long-term crutch
More exhaustive test matrix increases CI time; nightly/weekly cadence chosen to balance coverage and runtime cost
